title: How VCs are celebrating Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO

Today was the day we’ve all been waiting for. Anthropic silenced the critics, at least for now. It's looking like one of the best venture outcomes ever, even though the biggest winners aren’t VCs.

How do you celebrate a multibillion-dollar return?

Hello. It’s Ben Bergman.

Bessemer’s Byron Deeter, Lightspeed’s Ravi Mhatre, and Menlo’s Matt Murphy were all at the Nasdaq today to ring in Anthropic’s wildly successful IPO. They each minted their firms billions of dollars on paper, some of the biggest VC gains in history. And what will they do to celebrate tonight? Wing it. 

“Believe it or not, we’re in New York, and we don’t have a reservation yet,” Murphy told me when we caught up on a brief phone call between his TV appearances and meetings with limited partners. “It’s a little bit ad hoc.” 

After today, they can certainly afford to slip the maître d some cash to score a table. Which one do you think will pick up the dinner tab?

Anthropic’s biggest winners are not VCs but Amazon, Google, and its seven cofounders. Anthropic’s Series B funding round was infamously led by FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, who is now serving a 25-year prison sentence and would have been sitting on more than $40 billion.

Nonetheless, Anthropic’s valuation has soared to such heights that it still ranks among the best, if not the best, venture outcomes of all time. Aside from the aforementioned trio, Iconiq, GIC, Coatue, Sequoia, Spark, and Founders Fund are among the firms that made billions. 

With such a long list of VCs who can brag about being early in Anthropic (even if they got in very late), it was a day of extreme FOMO for those who never invested or gave up the chance at a billion dollars because of their ex.

As for the VC trio, Murphy said they plan to eat some steak and enjoy a few glasses of wine before heading to the Morgan Stanley party, one of several banks that are celebrating tonight. He said Anthropic itself is not hosting a public celebration. 

“A lot of the team is worn out from the IPO and headed back to their families and their jobs,” he said. “There's more recursive intelligence to be built, apparently.”

Read more

The buzz

Katie here. It’s hard to believe that the Anthropic IPO was almost overshadowed by another AI industry event, but the drama around Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia diverted a lot of industry attention. Most VCs I spoke to seem broadly in favor of Huang's return, given their general support for transformative founders. He also played a major role in the ecosystem by investing in and acquiring AI startups. 

Yet Huang has an uphill battle, with ongoing investigations into his alleged misconduct with a possible spy. The board also maintains that Huang will not be offered his job back. However, there’s one caveat. Huang has the power to add two new board members. It remains to be seen whether he will proceed with that option and if that will be enough to tip the balance in his favor. This drama feels far from over. 

Post of the week

There’s something poetic about rain in Silicon Valley on the eve of a massive liquidity event. 🌧️💰

— Adam Nash (@adamnash), November 18, 2026.

Around the cap table

  • Anthropic's IPO is set to make its cofounders, execs, and backers extremely rich. Here's who stands to gain the most.
  • Serena Williams is partnering with longtime investor Beth Ferreira to launch a new VC firm, Starfire Ventures. 
  • Nvidia is telling the robotics startups it has invested in that it still has their backs.
  • Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion.

Anthropic’s biggest winners are not VCs but Amazon, Google, and its seven cofounders. Anthropic’s Series B funding round was infamously led by FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried, who is now serving a 25-year prison sentence and would have been sitting on more than $40 billion.

Nonetheless, Anthropic’s valuation has soared to such heights that it still ranks among the best, if not the best, venture outcomes of all time. Aside from the aforementioned trio, Iconiq, GIC, Coatue, Sequoia, Spark, and Founders Fund are among the firms that made billions.

With such a long list of VCs who can brag about being early in Anthropic (even if they got in very late), it was a day of extreme FOMO for those who never invested or gave up the chance at a billion dollars because of their ex.

As for the VC trio, Murphy said they plan to eat some steak and enjoy a few glasses of wine before heading to the Morgan Stanley party, one of several banks that are celebrating tonight. He said Anthropic itself is not hosting a public celebration.

“A lot of the team is worn out from the IPO and headed back to their families and their jobs,” he said. “There's more recursive intelligence to be built, apparently.”

The buzz

Katie here. It’s hard to believe that the Anthropic IPO was almost overshadowed by another AI industry event, but the drama around Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia diverted a lot of industry attention. Most VCs I spoke to seem broadly in favor of Huang's return, given their general support for transformative founders. He also played a major role in the ecosystem by investing in and acquiring AI startups.

Yet Huang has an uphill battle, with ongoing investigations into his alleged misconduct with a possible spy. The board also maintains that Huang will not be offered his job back. However, there’s one caveat. Huang has the power to add two new board members. It remains to be seen whether he will proceed with that option and if that will be enough to tip the balance in his favor. This drama feels far from over.
